scope: Local T-shirt, sweatshirt and hoodie 3D preview improvements based on the three supplied front product photographs.
changes: Supplier-style hanging silhouettes and sleeve proportions
Raised, lined hood with a rounded crown and short tied cords
7 cm ribbed waistbands, 6.5 cm sleeve cuffs, broader ribbed crew necks
Shoulder and armhole seams, paired T-shirt hem stitches, pocket topstitch and entry welts
Physical-scale cotton and rib knit UVs independent of the print template
Cotton fibre sheen, neutral studio lights, soft contact shadows, highlight compression
Separate hood cavity occlusion prevents thin-layer shadow bands
Shadow textures are disposed when the product preview closes

neighboringChecks.scope: Earlier iteration, before the last garment-only refinements; final garment/viewer checks are listed separately.

runnerNote: npm test wrapper later could not create disposable Postgres because the local Docker disk was full. The rendering tests listed here are database-free and were run directly. No hosted database or alternate database was used; Docker data was not deleted.
visualChecks: White M: plain front, printed front and angle, blank reverse
Black M: plain and printed front
White M: T-shirt and hood front/side/back detail views
Browser pull demonstrations for all three garments
No browser console or shader errors

browserCpuPulls.units: milliseconds, CPU advance and mesh update only; no GPU timing

limitations: Procedural garment reconstruction from front photographs; unseen reverse folds are inferred, not a product scan.
Cloth motion remains a supported hanging approximation, not measured fabric simulation.
No claim of pixel-identical photographic reconstruction.
preserved: All 38 provider variants and supplier size measurements
Fixed physical front print dimensions and unprinted reverse
Receipt, checkout, payment and persistence behavior
